blocks.h2: Should a Condo Buyer Scope the Sewer?
blocks.body: In a small Lincoln Park condo building, the sewer lateral is usually a common element, so a big repair can become a special assessment for every owner. Before you buy, ask the association whether the line has been scoped recently. If not, a camera inspection can show whether it's in good shape or headed for repair. That's useful for buyers, and for boards planning reserves.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a Sewer Inspection
blocks.body: Access and line length matter most. A clear basement cleanout is simplest. A blocked line needs clearing first. We quote a flat price before we start.

blocks.h2: Sewer Camera Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Should I scope the sewer before buying a Lincoln Park home?
items.answer: Yes. A standard home inspection doesn't include the sewer, and a repair under an older building can be significant.

items.q: Can you inspect the line under the basement slab?
items.answer: Yes. The camera follows the line under the slab and out to the city sewer.

items.q: Can the camera show if the problem is in the city's sewer?
items.answer: Yes. We follow the line to the main and show you where the problem is.
Yes. You can share it with a seller, an agent or a condo board.

items.q: Can the association schedule a scope for the building?
items.answer: Yes. Many boards scope the line every few years.

items.q: Can you inspect a line that serves several units?
items.answer: Yes, from the basement cleanout to the city sewer.
